definition_zh: 合理地；相当地；以公道价格
definition_en: in a fair and sensible way; to a moderate degree; at a fair price
core_image: 天平两端轻轻持平，价钱与品质对得上
scene: 旧书店的柜台前，顾客翻看价签，觉得价钱与书况相称。The shop sells reasonably priced second-hand books.
sceneCN: 这里 reasonably 修饰 priced，是「以公道价格」（第 3 个义项：价钱合理）；句意为这家店卖的二手书价格公道。画面里可留意：持平的天平、与书况相称的价签。

pos.zh: 合理地；相当地；以公道价格

senses.title: In a fair and sensible way
senses.definition: in a way that is fair, sensible, and based on good judgment
senses.definitionCN: 以公平、明智且基于良好判断的方式
senses.example: She reasonably refused the unfair offer.
senses.exampleCN: 她合理地拒绝了那个不公平的提议。
senses.why: Reason is the base, and the suffix -able marks what fits reason, so the adverb describes acting in line with reason.
senses.whyCN: reason 是词根，后缀 -able 表示「合乎理性的」，因此这个副词描述按理性行事。

senses.title: To a moderate degree
senses.definition: to a fair but not extreme degree, more than a little
senses.definitionCN: 达到公道而不极端的程度，多于一点
senses.example: The exam was reasonably difficult.
senses.exampleCN: 这次考试相当难。
senses.why: Fairness of judgment weakened into fairness of degree, so the word came to mean fairly or quite.
senses.whyCN: 判断上的「公道」弱化为程度上的「适中」，于是这个词有了「相当」的意思。

senses.title: At a fair price
senses.definition: at a price that is fair for what is offered
senses.definitionCN: 以对所提供之物而言公道的价格
senses.example: The flat is reasonably priced for the area.
senses.exampleCN: 就这个地段而言，这套公寓价格公道。
senses.why: A price judged fair by reason is a price that reason approves, so the adverb commonly attaches to the word priced.
senses.whyCN: 经理性判定为公道的价格，就是理性认可的价格，因此这个副词常与 priced 连用。

intro.en: Reasonably grows from the Latin root for reckoning, passing through French into English and taking two suffixes, one for fitness and one for manner.
intro.cn: reasonably 从拉丁语「计算」的词根出发，经法语进入英语，并加上两个后缀：一个表「合乎」，一个表方式。

items.en: Ratio meant reckoning or account, the root of reason and of every fair judgment.
items.cn: ratio 意为计算或账目，是 reason 与一切公道判断的词根。

items.en: Old French raison carried the Latin root into English as reason, the power to judge.
items.cn: 古法语 raison 把拉丁词根带入英语，成为 reason，即判断的能力。

items.en: The suffix -able, from Latin -abilis, means capable of or fit for, giving reasonable.
items.cn: 后缀 -able 源自拉丁 -abilis，意为「能够……的、合乎……的」，由此构成 reasonable。

items.en: The native suffix -ly turns the adjective into an adverb of manner and degree.
items.cn: 本族后缀 -ly 把形容词变为表方式与程度的副词。

items.en: Modern English uses reasonably for fair judgment, for a moderate degree, and for a fair price.
items.cn: 现代英语用 reasonably 表公道判断、表适中程度，也表公道的价格。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adjective base and two related forms; the near-meaning group gathers degree words and words of fairness.
note.cn: 形近组收形容词原形与两个同族词；近义组收程度词与表公道的词。

entries.definition: Sensible and fair, the adjective base.
entries.definitionCN: 明智而公道的，形容词原形。

entries.definition: The power to think and judge.
In a practical and wise way.

normalIntro.en: The word is reason plus able plus ly: a judgment that fits reason, delivered in a fair manner.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 reason 加 able 再加 ly：合乎理性的判断，以公道的方式做出。

normal.en: Reason is the root; reasonable adds -able; reasonably adds -ly.
normal.cn: 词根是 reason，加 able 成 reasonable，再加 ly 成 reasonably。

normal.en: A reasonably priced item is priced in a way reason approves.
normal.cn: reasonably priced 指价格经得起理性衡量。

normal.en: Reasonably well means fairly well, not very well.
normal.cn: reasonably well 指相当好，而不是非常好。

normal.en: The -ly ending tells you the word describes how something is done.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ly 提醒你这个词描述做事的方式。

normal.en: Split it as reason + able + ly to keep the spelling right.
normal.cn: 把它拆成 reason 加 able 加 ly，拼写就不容易错。

abstract.en: Reasonableness is a scale: fair first, then moderate, never extreme.
abstract.cn: 合理性是一把尺：先讲公道，再讲适中，从不走极端。

abstract.en: To act reasonably is to leave room for the other side.
abstract.cn: 行事合理，就是给对方留出余地。

abstract.en: A fair price is reason made visible in numbers.
abstract.cn: 公道的价格，是理性在数字上的显形。

examples.en: She reasonably refused the unfair offer.
examples.cn: 她合理地拒绝了那个不公平的提议。

examples.en: The exam was reasonably difficult.
examples.cn: 这次考试相当难。

examples.en: The flat is reasonably priced for the area.
examples.cn: 就这个地段而言，这套公寓价格公道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 reason（理性）加 able（能）加 ly（地）：能按理性来，就是合理地；程度适中，就是相当地。

root: 拉丁 ratio（计算、账目）→ 古法语 raison → 英语 reason（理性）→ reasonable（合理的）→ reasonably（合理地）；同族有 reasoning、reasonableness。

sensesIntro.en: The core is judgment by reason; the senses move from a fair manner to a moderate degree to a fair price.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「按理性判断」；义项从公道行事，到适中程度，再到公道价格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance whose two pans rest level, price matching quality.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平两端持平，价钱与品质相称。

branches.en: a judgment weighed on a balance
a needle resting mid-scale
a price tag that matches the goods
fair in manner and moderate in degree
a moderate amount and a fair price

intro.en: The word grows from the Latin root for reckoning through two English suffixes, one for fitness and one for manner.
intro.cn: 这个词从拉丁语「计算」的词根出发，经过两个英语后缀：一个表「合乎」，一个表方式。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin ratio, and the suffix -able goes back to Latin -abilis.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是拉丁 ratio，后缀 -able 可追溯到拉丁 -abilis。

definition_zh: 反叛者；武装反抗；抗拒常规
definition_en: a person who rises against authority; to rise against authority; to refuse accepted rules
core_image: 举着火把的人群背对王座站成一排
scene: 广场上人群举着火把，把印着徽章的旗帜倒转过来。The rebel forces refused to surrender.
sceneCN: 这里 rebel 作定语，指「反叛者」（第 1 个义项：拿起武器反叛的人）；句意为叛军拒绝投降。画面里可留意：倒转的旗帜、背对王座的人群。

senses.title: A person who rises against authority
senses.definition: a person who takes up arms or openly refuses to obey those in power
senses.definitionCN: 拿起武器或公开拒绝服从当权者的人
senses.example: The rebel was arrested at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 那名反叛者在黎明时被捕。
senses.why: The Latin rebellis meant one who renews war, and the noun kept that image of a person who reopens a fight.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 rebellis 意为重新开战的人，名词保留了「重新掀起战斗」这一意象。

senses.title: To rise against authority
senses.definition: to fight against a government or a ruling power
senses.definitionCN: 与政府或统治力量作战
senses.example: The peasants rebelled against the heavy taxes.
senses.exampleCN: 农民们反抗沉重的赋税。
senses.why: The verb was formed from the noun, turning the person who renews war into the act of renewing it.
senses.whyCN: 动词由名词而来，把「重新开战的人」转成了「重新开战」这一行为。

senses.title: To resist accepted rules
senses.definition: to refuse to accept the habits or rules of a group, often in a personal way
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝接受某个群体的习惯或规则，常带个人色彩
senses.example: Teenagers often rebel against their parents' advice.
senses.exampleCN: 青少年常常抗拒父母的建议。
senses.why: Rebellion moved from the battlefield into daily life, where refusing advice is a small war of one's own.
senses.whyCN: 反叛从战场走进日常生活，拒绝建议就是一个人自己的小战争。

intro.en: Rebel carries war inside it: a Latin word for war sits at its centre, joined to a prefix meaning again.
intro.cn: rebel 内部藏着战争：拉丁语的「战争」一词就在它中间，并与表「再次」的前缀相连。

items.en: Bellum meant war, the raw material of every rebellion.
items.cn: bellum 意为战争，是一切反叛的原材料。

items.en: The prefix re- added the idea of again or in return, giving renewed war.
items.cn: 前缀 re- 加上「再次」或「回击」的意思，构成「重新开战」。

items.en: Rebellis described both a renewed war and the person who waged it.
items.cn: rebellis 既指重新开战的战争，也指发动它的人。

items.en: Old French rebelle carried the person and the act into English.
items.cn: 古法语 rebelle 把人与其行为一起带入英语。

items.en: Modern English uses rebel for the person, for the act, and for a personal refusal of rules.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rebel 指人、指行为，也指个人对规则的抗拒。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs and nouns close in spelling; the near-meaning group gathers words for armed and unarmed resistance.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写相近的动词与名词；近义组收表武装与非武装抵抗的词。

entries.definition: To drive back or push away.
One who rises in armed revolt.

normalIntro.en: The word keeps the Latin word for war at its centre, so every sense carries a small battlefield.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词中间藏着拉丁语的「战争」，因此每个义项都带着一小片战场。

normal.en: Re plus bellum: making war again is the oldest picture of a rebel.
normal.cn: re 加 bellum：重新开战，就是 rebel 最古老的画面。

normal.en: A rebel can be a person or an act, so one spelling serves noun and verb.
normal.cn: rebel 既可指人也可指行为，同一拼写兼作名词与动词。

normal.en: The noun stress falls on the first syllable, the verb stress on the second.
normal.cn: 名词重音在第一音节，动词重音在第二音节。

normal.en: Rebel against is the phrase for refusing a person or a rule.
normal.cn: rebel against 是拒绝某人或某条规则的固定搭配。

normal.en: Rebellion and rebellious grow from the same root, one an act and one a trait.
normal.cn: rebellion 与 rebellious 同根，一个指行为，一个指性格。

abstract.en: Every rebel begins by deciding that an old order no longer deserves obedience.
abstract.cn: 每个反叛者都从判定旧秩序不再值得服从开始。

abstract.en: Rebellion is renewal with a cost, a war fought again in a smaller room.
abstract.cn: 反叛是带代价的更新，是在更小的房间里再打一场战争。

abstract.en: To rebel against advice is to claim the right to make one's own mistakes.
abstract.cn: 抗拒建议，就是主张自己犯错的权利。

examples.en: The rebel was arrested at dawn.
examples.cn: 那名反叛者在黎明时被捕。

examples.en: The peasants rebelled against the heavy taxes.
examples.cn: 农民们反抗沉重的赋税。

examples.en: Teenagers often rebel against their parents' advice.
examples.cn: 青少年常常抗拒父母的建议。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（再）加 bellum（战争）：再开一战的人就是 rebel——反叛者；动词就是反抗。

root: 拉丁 bellum（战争）→ 前缀 re-（再次）→ 拉丁 rebellis（重新开战者）→ 古法语 rebelle → 英语 rebel；同族有 rebellion、rebellious。

sensesIntro.en: The core is renewed war; the senses cover the person, the act, and the everyday refusal of rules.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「重新开战」；义项覆盖人、行为，以及日常对规则的抗拒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd holding torches, standing with its back to a throne.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群举着火把，背对王座站成一排。

branches.en: a figure with a raised torch
a village rising in arms
a teenager turning away from advice
the person and the uprising
public war and private refusal
branches.cn: 公开的战争与私人的拒绝

intro.en: The word joins a Latin prefix to the Latin word for war, then passes through French into English.
intro.cn: 这个词把拉丁前缀与拉丁语的「战争」结合，再经法语进入英语。

latinIntro.en: Its Latin base is bellum, war, with the prefix re- meaning again.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 bellum（战争），前缀 re- 意为「再次」。

definition_en: to build again what was destroyed; to restore a system or feeling; to assemble something anew
core_image: 废墟上第一块新砖被稳稳放下
scene: 地震过后，工人在断裂的墙边重新砌起第一层砖。Crews began to rebuild the damaged school.
sceneCN: 这里 rebuild 是「重建」（第 1 个义项：重新建造被毁之物）；句意为施工队开始重建受损的学校。画面里可留意：废墟旁的新砖、断裂的墙。

senses.title: To build again what was destroyed
senses.definition: to construct again something that has been damaged or destroyed
senses.definitionCN: 重新建造被损坏或被毁的东西
senses.example: Crews began to rebuild the damaged school.
senses.exampleCN: 施工队开始重建受损的学校。
senses.why: The prefix re- means again, and build is the old verb for raising a structure, so rebuild is literally to raise it a second time.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 re- 意为「再次」，build 是「建造」的古动词，因此 rebuild 字面就是「再造一次」。

senses.title: To restore a system or feeling
senses.definition: to bring back the strength of an economy, an organization, or a relationship
senses.definitionCN: 恢复经济、组织或关系的力量
senses.example: The new coach helped rebuild the team's confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 新教练帮助球队重建了信心。
senses.why: A structure and a relationship share the same frame, so building again became a metaphor for restoring strength.
senses.whyCN: 建筑与人际关系共用同一框架，于是「再建一次」成了「恢复力量」的隐喻。

senses.title: To put together anew
senses.definition: to assemble something again from its parts, often in a new form
senses.definitionCN: 把事物的各部分重新组装，常以新形态呈现
senses.example: Engineers had to rebuild the engine from spare parts.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师不得不用备用零件重新组装发动机。
senses.why: The prefix adds repetition rather than repair, so the word also covers taking something apart and assembling it again.
senses.whyCN: 这个前缀带来的是重复而非修理，所以这个词也涵盖拆开再组装。

intro.en: Rebuild joins a Latin prefix of repetition to a native English verb of construction, and then extends the image from walls to people.
intro.cn: rebuild 把表重复的拉丁前缀与英语本族的「建造」动词结合，再把这一形象从墙延伸到人。

items.en: Byldan meant to build or to dwell, the native verb behind build.
items.cn: byldan 意为建造或居住，是 build 背后的本族动词。

items.en: The Latin prefix re- added the idea of again to the verb.
items.cn: 拉丁前缀 re- 为这个动词加上「再次」的意思。

items.en: Middle English rebuilden joined prefix and verb into a single word.
items.cn: 中古英语 rebuilden 把前缀与动词合成一个词。

items.en: Modern English extended rebuild from houses to systems, teams, and feelings.
items.cn: 现代英语把 rebuild 从房屋扩展到系统、团队与情感。

items.en: Rebuilding confidence borrows the image of a structure raised again.
items.cn: 重建信心借用了「结构再立一次」的形象。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short verbs beginning with re-; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of restoring and assembling.
note.cn: 形近组收以 re- 开头的短动词；近义组收表恢复与组装的动词。

entries.definition: To bring back a former state.
To repair and modernise a building.

normalIntro.en: The word is simply again plus build, and the picture of a second raising runs through every sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是「再次」加「建造」，而「再立一次」的画面贯穿所有义项。

normal.en: Re plus build: build it once more, and you have rebuilt it.
normal.cn: re 加 build：再建一次，就是 rebuild。

normal.en: Rebuilt is the past form, so the pattern is rebuild, rebuilt, rebuilt.
normal.cn: 过去式是 rebuilt，变化模式是 rebuild、rebuilt、rebuilt。

normal.en: Rebuild trust and rebuild a bridge use the same verb in two scales.
normal.cn: rebuild trust 与 rebuild a bridge 是同一个动词的两种尺度。

normal.en: From scratch is a common partner, meaning with nothing left to reuse.
normal.cn: from scratch 是常见搭配，意为没有可再利用的东西。

normal.en: The stress falls on the second syllable, after the weak re-.
normal.cn: 重音落在第二音节，在轻读的 re- 之后。

abstract.en: What is rebuilt is not the old thing but a new thing in the old place.
abstract.cn: 重建的并不是旧物，而是在旧地点的新的东西。

abstract.en: Repair fixes a crack; rebuilding accepts that the crack cannot be fixed.
abstract.cn: 修理补一道缝，重建则承认那道缝已无法修补。

abstract.en: A person who rebuilds is betting that the future is worth the labour.
abstract.cn: 选择重建的人，是在赌未来值得这份劳作。

examples.en: Crews began to rebuild the damaged school.
examples.cn: 施工队开始重建受损的学校。

examples.en: The new coach helped rebuild the team's confidence.
examples.cn: 新教练帮助球队重建了信心。

examples.en: Engineers had to rebuild the engine from spare parts.
examples.cn: 工程师不得不用备用零件重新组装发动机。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（再）加 build（建造）：再建一次就是重建；把信心、经济再建起来，也是 rebuild。

root: 古英语 byldan（建造）+ 前缀 re-（再次）→ 中古英语 rebuilden → 现代英语 rebuild；同族有 rebuilt、rebuilding。

sensesIntro.en: The core is raising a structure a second time; the senses extend from buildings to systems and to assemblies.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把结构再立一次」；义项从建筑延伸到系统与组装。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first new brick laid on a field of rubble.
core.cn: 核心意象：废墟上放下第一块新砖。

branches.en: a brick laid on rubble
a team finding its confidence
an engine taken apart and refitted
stone and spirit rebuilt
a system and a machine reassembled
branches.cn: 系统与机器被重新组装

intro.en: A Latin prefix of repetition meets a native English building verb, which gives the word its simple shape.
intro.cn: 一个表重复的拉丁前缀遇上英语本族的建造动词，构成了这个词的简单外形。

latinIntro.en: The only Latin element is the prefix re-, meaning again or back; build itself is native English.
latinIntro.cn: 唯一的拉丁元素是前缀 re-，意为「再次、回」；build 本身是英语本族词。

definition_zh: 回忆起；召回；撤销；记忆力
definition_en: to remember something from the past; to order a person or product back; to cancel officially; the power to remember
core_image: 一只手指向身后，把远处的画面拉回眼前
scene: 老人翻开旧相册，指着一张褪色的照片停住。She could still recall the smell of her grandmother's kitchen.
sceneCN: 这里 recall 是「回忆起」（第 1 个义项：把过去的记忆唤回）；句意为她仍能回忆起祖母厨房里的味道。画面里可留意：翻开的相册、褪色的照片。

senses.title: To remember
senses.definition: to bring a past event or detail back into the mind
senses.definitionCN: 把过去的事件或细节重新带回心里
senses.example: She could still recall the smell of her grandmother's kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 她仍能回忆起祖母厨房里的味道。
senses.why: Re- means back, and call means to summon, so the word pictures a memory being called back to the present.
senses.whyCN: re- 意为「回」，call 意为「召唤」，因此这个词描绘记忆被唤回当下。

senses.title: To call back
senses.definition: to order a person or a product to return
senses.definitionCN: 命令某个人或某件产品返回
senses.example: The company recalled thousands of faulty toys.
senses.exampleCN: 公司召回了数千件有缺陷的玩具。
senses.why: The literal image of calling someone back became an official order to return, first for envoys and later for goods.
senses.whyCN: 把某人唤回的字面形象，变成了正式的返回命令，先是针对使节，后来针对商品。

senses.title: To cancel officially
senses.definition: to withdraw a decision, an offer, or a law by official action
senses.definitionCN: 以官方行动撤回决定、提议或法律
senses.example: The council recalled the unpopular rule.
senses.exampleCN: 议会撤销了那条不受欢迎的规定。
senses.why: A cancelled decision is sent back to those who made it, and the image of calling back covers that reversal.
senses.whyCN: 被撤销的决定被送回做出决定的人那里，而「唤回」的形象正涵盖这种反转。

senses.title: The power to remember
senses.definition: the ability to remember things, used as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 记住事物的能力，作名词使用
senses.example: His recall of names is remarkably quick.
senses.exampleCN: 他记名字的速度快得惊人。
senses.why: When the act of calling back is viewed as a capacity, the verb turns into a noun naming memory itself.
senses.whyCN: 当「唤回」这一行为被视为一种能力时，动词就转为指称记忆本身的名词。

intro.en: Recall is a native calling verb with a Latin prefix: to call back is first a voice, then a memory, then an order.
intro.cn: recall 是本族的「呼喊」动词加拉丁前缀：唤回先是声音，再是记忆，最后是命令。

items.en: Ceallian meant to call out, the native verb behind call.
items.cn: ceallian 意为呼喊，是 call 背后的本族动词。

items.en: Norse kalla, to call, reinforced the same verb in northern English.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 kalla（呼喊）在英格兰北部强化了同一个动词。

items.en: The Latin prefix re-, meaning back, joined call to make recall.
items.cn: 拉丁前缀 re- 意为「回」，与 call 结合成 recall。

items.en: Middle English recallen meant both to call back and to remember.
items.cn: 中古英语 recallen 既指唤回，也指记起。

items.en: Modern English extended recall to products, officials, and the noun for memory.
items.cn: 现代英语把 recall 扩展到产品、官员，以及表记忆的名词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs with a similar opening; the near-meaning group gathers words for remembering and for summoning back.
note.cn: 形近组收开头相似的动词；近义组收表记忆与唤回的词。

entries.definition: To keep or bring back in mind.
To gather memories back with effort.

normalIntro.en: The word is call plus back: a voice calls, and what was distant returns.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 call 加「回」：声音一唤，远处的东西就回来。

normal.en: Re plus call: to call back a face, a product, or a rule.
normal.cn: re 加 call：把面孔、产品或规定唤回来。

normal.en: Recall a memory is the everyday sense; product recall is the official one.
normal.cn: recall a memory 是日常义；product recall 是官方义。

normal.en: The noun has the same spelling, so recall can name the power to remember.
normal.cn: 名词拼写相同，因此 recall 也能指记忆力。

normal.en: Beyond recall means so far gone that it cannot be called back.
normal.cn: beyond recall 意为久远到再也唤不回来。

normal.en: Keep the double l: recall, recalled, recalling.
normal.cn: 注意双写 l：recall、recalled、recalling。

abstract.en: Memory is a call across time, and the past answers only if it still lives in us.
abstract.cn: 记忆是穿越时间的一次呼唤，过去只有在仍活在我们心里时才会应答。

abstract.en: A recall of a product is an admission that something once sold should not have been.
abstract.cn: 召回产品，就是承认某件已售出之物本不该售出。

abstract.en: What a society chooses to recall is what it chooses to be.
abstract.cn: 一个社会选择记住什么，就是选择成为什么。

examples.en: She could still recall the smell of her grandmother's kitchen.
examples.cn: 她仍能回忆起祖母厨房里的味道。

examples.en: The company recalled thousands of faulty toys.
examples.cn: 公司召回了数千件有缺陷的玩具。

examples.en: His recall of names is remarkably quick.
examples.cn: 他记名字的速度快得惊人。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（回）加 call（呼唤）：把记忆唤回来就是回忆；把人或产品唤回来就是召回。

root: 古英语 ceallian / 古诺斯语 kalla（呼喊）+ 前缀 re-（回）→ 中古英语 recallen → 现代英语 recall；同族有 recalling、recallable。

sensesIntro.en: The core is calling something back; the senses move from memory to products, to cancelled decisions, and to memory as a power.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把东西唤回」；义项从记忆，到产品，到被撤销的决定，最后到作为一种能力的记忆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pointing backwards, pulling a distant scene into view.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手指向身后，把远处的画面拉回眼前。

branches.en: a face rising from an old photograph
branches.cn: 一张脸从旧照片里浮起

branches.en: toys pulled from shop shelves
a rule struck from the book
branches.cn: 一条规定被从册子上划去

branches.en: a quick list of names in the mind
branches.cn: 脑中飞快列出的一串名字

branches.en: a memory called back and a decision called back

intro.en: A native English verb of calling takes a Latin prefix, and the resulting word spreads from voices to memories and to official orders.
intro.cn: 英语本族的「呼喊」动词接上拉丁前缀，所得之词从声音扩展到记忆与官方命令。

latinIntro.en: The Latin element is the prefix re-, meaning back; the verb call is native English.
latinIntro.cn: 其中的拉丁元素是前缀 re-，意为「回」；动词 call 是英语本族词。

definition_en: a written proof of payment; the act of receiving; an old word for a recipe or formula
core_image: 一张薄纸从柜台递过来，上面印着金额
scene: 顾客把零钱收进钱包，店员递来一张打印的小票。Please keep the receipt in case you need to return the item.
sceneCN: 这里 receipt 是「收据」（第 1 个义项：付款的书面凭证）；句意为请保留收据，以便日后需要退货。画面里可留意：柜台递来的小票、打印的金额。

senses.title: A written proof of payment
senses.definition: a piece of paper that shows money or goods have been received
senses.definitionCN: 证明款项或货物已被收到的纸片
senses.example: Please keep the receipt in case you need to return the item.
senses.exampleCN: 请保留收据，以便日后需要退货。
senses.why: The word began as the act of receiving and then came to name the paper that proves the act.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初指「收到」这一行为，后来指证明该行为的纸片。

senses.title: The act of receiving
senses.definition: the act or fact of taking something that has been sent or given
senses.definitionCN: 接收已寄出或给予之物的行为或事实
senses.example: The receipt of the parcel was delayed by snow.
senses.exampleCN: 由于下雪，包裹的收取被延误了。
senses.why: Latin receptus, the past participle of recipere, named the act of taking something in, and English kept that abstract sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 receptus 是 recipere 的过去分词，指「收进」这一行为，英语保留了这层抽象含义。

senses.title: An old word for a recipe
senses.definition: a written formula for preparing something, still used in pharmacy
senses.definitionCN: 制备某物的书面配方，药房仍在使用
senses.example: The old receipt for cough syrup is still in the family book.
senses.exampleCN: 那张治咳嗽糖浆的老配方还夹在家庭记事本里。
senses.why: Before recipe took over the kitchen, receipt named any written formula, and pharmacy kept the older word.
senses.whyCN: 在 recipe 接管厨房之前，receipt 指任何书面配方，药房一直保留这个更旧的词。

intro.en: Receipt begins as an act of taking, becomes a note about that act, and keeps an old sense of a written formula.
intro.cn: receipt 从「拿取」这一行为开始，变成关于该行为的字据，并保留了「书面配方」的旧义。

items.en: Recipere meant to take back or receive, built from re- and capere, to take.
items.cn: recipere 意为收回或接收，由 re- 与 capere（拿取）构成。

items.en: Receptus, its past participle, named the thing or act received.
items.cn: 其过去分词 receptus 指被接收之物或接收这一行为。

items.en: Old French receite carried the word into English as a note of what was received.
items.cn: 古法语 receite 把这个词带入英语，指收到之物的字据。

items.en: English scholars later restored the silent p to honour the Latin root.
items.cn: 英语学者后来补回不发音的 p，以呼应拉丁词根。

items.en: Modern English uses receipt for proof of payment, for the act of receiving, and for an old formula.
items.cn: 现代英语用 receipt 指付款凭证、收取行为，也指旧式配方。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the same long vowel; the near-meaning group gathers papers that record a transaction.
note.cn: 形近组收同样带长元音的词；近义组收记录交易的各类纸据。

entries.definition: A paper that can be exchanged for goods.
A bill listing goods and their price.

normalIntro.en: The word is a paper proof born from the act of receiving, with a silent p left over from Latin.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是由「收到」这一行为产生的纸面凭证，还留着从拉丁语来的不发音 p。

normal.en: The p in receipt is silent, so it sounds like re-seat.
normal.cn: receipt 里的 p 不发音，听起来像 re-seat。

normal.en: Keep the receipt is what a shop assistant says after payment.
normal.cn: Keep the receipt 是店员收款后常说的话。

normal.en: A receipt proves you paid; a recipe tells you how to cook.
normal.cn: receipt 证明你付过钱，recipe 告诉你怎样做菜。

normal.en: On receipt of means at the moment something arrives.
normal.cn: on receipt of 意为在某物到达的那一刻。

normal.en: The plural simply adds s, but the p stays silent.
normal.cn: 复数只加 s，但 p 依然不发音。

abstract.en: A receipt is trust made portable, a small proof you can carry away.
abstract.cn: 收据是可以带走的信任，是一份能随身携带的证明。

abstract.en: What is written down becomes a claim; what is not may be denied.
abstract.cn: 写下来的才成为凭据，没写下来的可能被否认。

abstract.en: Every receipt records a moment when two people agreed on a value.
abstract.cn: 每一张收据都记录着两个人就某个价值达成一致的瞬间。

examples.en: Please keep the receipt in case you need to return the item.
examples.cn: 请保留收据，以便日后需要退货。

examples.en: The receipt of the parcel was delayed by snow.
examples.cn: 由于下雪，包裹的收取被延误了。

examples.en: The old receipt for cough syrup is still in the family book.
examples.cn: 那张治咳嗽糖浆的老配方还夹在家庭记事本里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「柜台递来一张纸」：付过钱，拿到凭证，就是收据；注意其中的 p 不发音。

root: 拉丁 recipere（收回、接收，re- 回 + capere 拿取）→ 拉丁 receptus → 古法语 receite → 英语 receipt（p 为后来按拉丁语复原的拼写）；同族有 receive、reception、recipient。

sensesIntro.en: The core is taking something in; the senses move from the act to the paper proof, and then to an old written formula.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把东西收进来」；义项从行为，到纸面凭证，再到旧式的书面配方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin slip of paper handed across a counter, the amount printed on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：柜台那边递来一张薄纸，上面印着金额。

branches.en: a slip handed over the counter
branches.cn: 从柜台递过来的一张纸

branches.en: a parcel arriving at the door
a formula written in an old book
paper proof and the act it records
branches.cn: 纸面凭证与它所记录的行为

branches.en: receiving a note and receiving a formula

intro.en: The word comes from the Latin verb of taking, through a French note, and keeps a Latin spelling mark.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语的「拿取」动词，经法语的字据用法而来，并保留了一个拉丁拼写标记。

latinIntro.en: Its Latin base is recipere, with re- meaning back and capere meaning to take.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 recipere，其中 re- 意为「回」，capere 意为「拿取」。

definition_en: to take into one's hands or possession; to welcome a guest; to pick up a signal; to experience something
core_image: 双手向前摊开，接住递来的东西
scene: 酒店门口，前台人员侧身让客人先进门。The hotel receives guests from all over the world.
sceneCN: 这里 receives 是「接待」（第 2 个义项：迎接客人）；句意为这家酒店接待来自世界各地的客人。画面里可留意：门口侧身让路的前台、摊开的双手。

senses.title: To get what is sent
senses.definition: to take into one's hands or possession something that has been sent or given
senses.definitionCN: 把寄来或给予的东西拿到手中或归于自己
senses.example: She received a letter from her old teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 她收到了老教师寄来的一封信。
senses.why: Recipere joined re-, back, and capere, to take, so the word pictures taking something that comes to you.
senses.whyCN: recipere 由 re-（回）与 capere（拿取）组成，因此这个词描绘把送到你面前的东西收下。

senses.title: To welcome a guest
senses.definition: to greet and welcome someone who arrives
senses.definitionCN: 迎接并款待到来的人
senses.example: The hotel receives guests from all over the world.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店接待来自世界各地的客人。
senses.why: A guest is also something that comes to you, so the same verb covers taking a person in.
senses.whyCN: 客人也是来到你面前的人，因此同一个动词也涵盖把一个人迎进来。

senses.title: To pick up a signal
senses.definition: to catch and translate a broadcast or electronic signal
senses.definitionCN: 捕捉并转换广播或电子信号
senses.example: The old radio can still receive short-wave signals.
senses.exampleCN: 这台旧收音机仍能接收短波信号。
senses.why: A message arriving through the air is taken in by the set, so the same verb covers signals.
senses.whyCN: 通过空气传来的信息被机器收进来，因此同一个动词也用于信号。

senses.title: To experience something
senses.definition: to be given a reaction, a treatment, or an impression
senses.definitionCN: 得到某种反应、对待或印象
senses.example: The plan received strong criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案受到了强烈的批评。
senses.why: To receive a reaction is to have it delivered to you, even when the thing delivered is unpleasant.
senses.whyCN: 受到某种反应，就是让反应落到自己身上，即使落到身上的东西并不愉快。

intro.en: Receive is a Latin taking verb that came through French, and its image of open hands extends to guests, signals, and reactions.
intro.cn: receive 是经法语传来的拉丁「拿取」动词，其「摊开双手」的形象延伸到客人、信号与反应。

items.en: Capere meant to take or seize, the core of the whole family.
items.cn: capere 意为拿取或抓住，是整个词族的核心。

items.en: Recipere added re-, back, to capere, giving the sense of taking something in.
items.cn: recipere 在 capere 前加 re-（回），得到「把东西收进来」的意思。

items.en: Old French receivre carried the verb into English with its broad sense of taking.
items.cn: 古法语 receivre 把这个动词带入英语，保留了宽泛的「拿取」义。

items.en: Middle English receiven already covered letters, guests, and blows.
items.cn: 中古英语 receiven 已涵盖信件、客人，以及打击。

items.en: Modern English added signals and medical treatment to the older range.
items.cn: 现代英语在旧有范围上又加入了信号与医疗。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs ending in the same sound; the near-meaning group gathers words of getting and welcoming.
note.cn: 形近组收相同结尾音的动词；近义组收表获得与迎接的词。

entries.definition: To make someone believe what is false.
To form an idea or a plan.
To get something, often with effort.

normalIntro.en: The word pictures open hands: whatever comes, a letter or a guest, is taken in.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词描绘摊开的双手：无论来的是信还是客人，都被收进来。

normal.en: Re plus ceive: to take back what was sent to you.
normal.cn: re 加 ceive：把寄给你的东西收下来。

normal.en: Received is the past form, so write receive, received, receiving.
normal.cn: 过去式是 received，拼写为 receive、received、receiving。

normal.en: Receive guests is the formal way to say welcome them.
normal.cn: receive guests 是「迎接客人」的正式说法。

normal.en: A radio receives a signal with no hands at all.
normal.cn: 收音机接收信号，完全不用手。

normal.en: Receive criticism uses the same verb as receive a gift.
normal.cn: receive criticism 与 receive a gift 用的是同一个动词。

abstract.en: To receive is to accept that something comes from outside oneself.
abstract.cn: 接收就是承认有些东西来自自身之外。

abstract.en: A receiver must be open; a closed hand receives nothing.
abstract.cn: 接收者必须敞开，握紧的手什么也接不到。

abstract.en: Receiving a reaction is the price of having acted at all.
abstract.cn: 受到反应，是曾经行动过的代价。

examples.en: She received a letter from her old teacher.
examples.cn: 她收到了老教师寄来的一封信。

examples.en: The hotel receives guests from all over the world.
examples.cn: 这家酒店接待来自世界各地的客人。

examples.en: The plan received strong criticism.
examples.cn: 这个方案受到了强烈的批评。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（回）加 ceive（拿取）：把送来的东西拿回来，就是收到；把客人迎进来，就是接待。

root: 拉丁 recipere（re- 回 + capere 拿取）→ 古法语 receivre → 中古英语 receiven → 英语 receive；同族有 receiver、reception、receipt。

sensesIntro.en: The core is taking something in; the senses move from things to guests, to signals, and to reactions.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把东西收进来」；义项从物品，到客人，到信号，再到反应。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two open hands catching what is handed over.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只摊开的手接住递来的东西。

branches.en: a letter placed in the palm
a guest stepping inside
an aerial picking up a wave
a harsh remark landing
branches.cn: 一句严厉的话落到身上

branches.en: a thing received and a person welcomed

intro.en: The family is built on the Latin verb for taking, with prefixes and English suffixes adding direction and agents.
intro.cn: 这个词族建立在拉丁语的「拿取」动词上，前缀与英语后缀补充方向与施动者。

latinIntro.en: The Latin core is capere, to take, with re- meaning back; French carried it to English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁核心是 capere（拿取），前缀 re- 意为「回」；法语把它带到英语。

items.meaning: one who or that which receives

definition_en: a device that picks up signals; a person who receives something; the part of a telephone held to the ear
core_image: 一只黑色盒子接着天线，指示灯亮起
scene: 桌上摆着一台老式收音机，金属旋钮旁的天线伸向窗外。He adjusted the receiver to catch a clearer signal.
sceneCN: 这里 receiver 是「接收器」（第 1 个义项：接收信号的设备）；句意为他把接收器调了调，想收到更清楚的信号。画面里可留意：伸向窗外的天线、亮起的指示灯。

senses.title: A device that picks up signals
senses.definition: an apparatus that catches and turns broadcast or electronic signals into sound or pictures
senses.definitionCN: 捕捉广播或电子信号并转成声音或图像的装置
senses.example: He adjusted the receiver to catch a clearer signal.
senses.exampleCN: 他把接收器调了调，想收到更清楚的信号。
senses.why: The suffix -er marks the doer, so a device that receives takes the same name as a person who receives.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -er 标记施动者，因此执行接收的设备与执行接收的人共用一个名称。

senses.title: A person who receives
senses.definition: a person to whom something is sent or given
senses.definitionCN: 某物被寄送或给予的对象
senses.example: The receiver must sign for the parcel.
senses.exampleCN: 收件人必须在包裹上签字。
senses.why: In law and post, the one who takes delivery is named by the act, and -er turns receive into that name.
senses.whyCN: -er 把 receive 变成施动名词，在法律与邮政用语中，收货的一方就以此命名。

senses.title: The telephone handset
senses.definition: the part of a telephone that is held to the ear and produces sound
senses.definitionCN: 电话中贴近耳朵并发出声音的部分
senses.example: She lifted the receiver and heard a dial tone.
senses.exampleCN: 她拿起听筒，听到了拨号音。
senses.why: The part held to the ear receives the voice, so the device took the name of what it does.
senses.whyCN: 贴近耳朵的部分负责接收声音，于是这件器件以其功能得名。

intro.en: Receiver is receive plus the agent suffix -er, and the same pattern names a machine, a person, and a telephone part.
intro.cn: receiver 是 receive 加施动后缀 -er，同一构词方式命名了机器、人，以及电话部件。

items.en: Recipere, to receive, came to English through French as receive.
items.cn: recipere（接收）经法语进入英语，成为 receive。

items.en: The native suffix -er marks the one who performs an action, giving receiver.
items.cn: 本族后缀 -er 标记执行动作的一方，由此构成 receiver。

items.en: Middle English receivere named a person who took something in.
items.cn: 中古英语 receivere 指收下某物的人。

items.en: With the telephone, the part held to the ear was called the receiver.
items.cn: 随着电话出现，贴近耳朵的部件被称为 receiver。

items.en: Radio and satellite sets borrowed the same word for the unit that catches signals.
items.cn: 收音机与卫星设备借用同一个词，指捕捉信号的装置。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers agent nouns from the same verb family; the near-meaning group gathers words for recipients and devices.
note.cn: 形近组收同一动词族里的施动名词；近义组收表收件人与设备的词。

entries.definition: A person who forms an idea.
The part of a phone held in the hand.

normalIntro.en: The word is receive plus -er: whatever does the receiving, person or machine, is a receiver.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 receive 加 -er：无论人或机器，只要做接收这件事，就是 receiver。

normal.en: Receive plus -er: the one that receives.
normal.cn: receive 加 -er：接收的那一方。

normal.en: A radio receiver catches signals; a telephone receiver catches a voice.
normal.cn: radio receiver 接收信号，telephone receiver 接收声音。

normal.en: A receiver of stolen goods is a person, not a machine.
normal.cn: receiver of stolen goods 指的是人，不是机器。

normal.en: The plural is receivers, with no change in the base.
normal.cn: 复数是 receivers，词干不变。

normal.en: Keep the ei in receive and the -er on the end.
normal.cn: 记住 receive 里的 ei 与词尾的 -er。

abstract.en: Every receiver defines a sender; the two are made for each other.
abstract.cn: 每一个接收者都定义了一个发送者，两者互为存在。

abstract.en: A receiver is powerful only when it is tuned to the right wave.
abstract.cn: 接收器只有调到正确的波长才有力量。

abstract.en: To be a receiver of kindness is to owe a return that may never come.
abstract.cn: 接受善意的人，欠下了一份也许永远不必偿还的回报。

examples.en: He adjusted the receiver to catch a clearer signal.
examples.cn: 他把接收器调了调，想收到更清楚的信号。

examples.en: The receiver must sign for the parcel.
examples.cn: 收件人必须在包裹上签字。

examples.en: She lifted the receiver and heard a dial tone.
examples.cn: 她拿起听筒，听到了拨号音。

dict_mnemonic.text: receive（接收）加 er（做某事的人或物）：会接收的东西就是接收器，接收的人就是收件人，电话上接收声音的就是听筒。

root: receive（收到）加后缀 -er（表施动者或工具）→ receiver；receive 源自拉丁 recipere；同族有 reception、receivable。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the one that receives; the senses split into a machine, a person, and a telephone part.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「负责接收的那一方」；义项分为机器、人，以及电话部件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a black box with an aerial, its indicator light glowing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只接着天线的黑盒子，指示灯亮起。

branches.en: a box with a glowing lamp
branches.cn: 一只亮着指示灯的盒子

branches.en: a hand signing for a parcel
a handset lifted to the ear
a machine and a person that receive
branches.cn: 接收的机器与接收的人

branches.en: a parcel taken and a voice heard

intro.en: The word is built with the agent suffix -er on the verb receive, and that shape serves both people and machines.
intro.cn: 这个词由动词 receive 加施动后缀 -er 构成，这一外形同时适用于人与机器。

latinIntro.en: The verb goes back to Latin recipere; the suffix -er is native English.
latinIntro.cn: 动词可追溯到拉丁 recipere；后缀 -er 是英语本族成分。

definition_en: happening or existing a short time ago; fresh and up to date; belonging to modern times
core_image: 日历上刚翻过的一页，墨迹还新
scene: 报纸头版印着前一天发生的事，纸边还带着油墨味。Recent research suggests that sleep affects memory.
sceneCN: 这里 recent 是「最近的」（第 1 个义项：不久前发生的）；句意为近期研究表明睡眠会影响记忆。画面里可留意：刚翻过的日历、带油墨味的报纸。

senses.title: Happening a short time ago
senses.definition: happening or existing only a short time before the present
senses.definitionCN: 在当下之前不久发生或存在的
senses.example: Recent research suggests that sleep affects memory.
senses.exampleCN: 近期研究表明睡眠会影响记忆。
senses.why: Latin recens meant fresh or just made, and English kept the sense of something still close in time.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 recens 意为新鲜的、刚做成的，英语保留了「在时间上仍然靠近」的含义。

senses.title: Fresh and up to date
senses.definition: containing the newest information and not yet replaced
senses.definitionCN: 包含最新信息、尚未被取代的
senses.example: The library keeps recent issues of the journal.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆保留了这份期刊最新的几期。
senses.why: What is fresh is also current, so the word came to describe information that has not been overtaken.
senses.whyCN: 新鲜的东西也是当下的，于是这个词用来形容尚未被超越的信息。

senses.title: Belonging to modern times
senses.definition: of a period close to the present, especially in history or geology
senses.definitionCN: 属于靠近当下的时期，尤其用于历史或地质分期
senses.example: Recent history covers the last two centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 近代史涵盖过去两个世纪。
senses.why: From a few days ago the word widened to a whole historical period that is close to the present.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从「几天前」扩展到整个靠近当下的历史时期。

intro.en: Recent comes straight from a Latin adjective of freshness, and its sense widened from fresh things to fresh time and fresh periods.
intro.cn: recent 直接来自拉丁语表「新鲜」的形容词，其含义从新鲜之物扩展到新鲜的时间与时期。

items.en: Recens meant fresh, new, or just made, said of things still new to the senses.
items.cn: recens 意为新鲜的、新的、刚做成的，用于感官上仍新的事物。

items.en: The comparative recentior meant more recent, the form behind the English degree forms.
items.cn: 比较级 recentior 意为「更近期的」，是英语比较形式的来源。

items.en: Old French recent brought the adjective into English unchanged in sense.
items.cn: 古法语 recent 把这个形容词原样带入英语，含义未变。

items.en: Middle English recent applied the word to events and to writing.
items.cn: 中古英语 recent 把这个词用于事件与文字。

items.en: Modern English extended recent to news, research, and whole historical periods.
items.cn: 现代英语把 recent 扩展到新闻、研究以及整个历史时期。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers adjectives close in sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for newness and currency.
note.cn: 形近组收读音相近的形容词；近义组收表新鲜与当下的词。

entries.definition: One who rules in another's place.
The most recent of a series.
Of the present or near past.

normalIntro.en: The word pictures something still warm from happening, like a page just turned.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词描绘刚刚发生、还带着热度的事物，像刚翻过的一页日历。

normal.en: Recent sounds like re-sent, as if news was just sent to you.
normal.cn: recent 听起来像 re-sent，仿佛消息刚刚发给你。

normal.en: In recent years is the standard phrase for the near past.
normal.cn: in recent years 是表达「近年来」的标准搭配。

normal.en: Recent research means work published not long ago.
normal.cn: recent research 指不久前发表的研究。

normal.en: The comparison uses more recent, not recenter.
normal.cn: 比较级用 more recent，而不是 recenter。

normal.en: Recent history is a period; a recent event is a moment.
normal.cn: recent history 是一段时期，a recent event 是一个瞬间。

abstract.en: The recent is the edge of time, where memory has not yet become history.
abstract.cn: 「最近的」是时间的边缘，记忆尚未变成历史。

abstract.en: What is recent feels important precisely because it is still warm.
abstract.cn: 刚发生的事显得重要，正因为它还带着温度。

abstract.en: Every age calls its own news recent and the rest old.
abstract.cn: 每个时代都把自己的新闻称为「最近的」，把其余称为旧的。

examples.en: Recent research suggests that sleep affects memory.
examples.cn: 近期研究表明睡眠会影响记忆。

examples.en: The library keeps recent issues of the journal.
examples.cn: 图书馆保留了这份期刊最新的几期。

examples.en: Recent history covers the last two centuries.
examples.cn: 近代史涵盖过去两个世纪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 recent 联想成「日历刚翻过去的一页」：墨迹还新，就是最近的。

root: 拉丁 recens（新鲜的、刚出现的）→ 古法语 recent → 中古英语 recent → 英语 recent；同族有 recently、recency、recentness。

sensesIntro.en: The core is freshness in time; the senses move from a recent event to current information and to a modern period.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「时间上的新鲜」；义项从刚发生的事，到当下的信息，再到近代时期。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a calendar page just turned, the ink still fresh.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历刚翻过的一页，墨迹还新。

branches.en: a newspaper from yesterday
a journal issue on the shelf
a chapter on the last two centuries
branches.cn: 讲述过去两个世纪的一章

branches.en: a recent event and recent data
branches.cn: 刚发生的事与最新的数据

branches.en: fresh news and modern history
branches.cn: 新鲜的新闻与近代的历史

intro.en: A short Latin adjective of freshness gives the base, and English endings produce the adverb and the nouns.
intro.cn: 一个表新鲜的简短拉丁形容词提供词根，英语词尾则造出副词与名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is recens, with the comparative recentior behind the English degree forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 recens，其比较级 recentior 是英语比较形式的来源。

definition_en: not long ago; during the period just before now; newly
core_image: 手机屏上一条刚收到的消息，时间标着「刚刚」
scene: 会议室的同事指着屏幕上刚发布的公告，语速很快。She recently joined the research team.
sceneCN: 这里 recently 是「最近」（第 1 个义项：不久前）；句意为她最近加入了研究团队。画面里可留意：刚收到的消息、屏幕上的公告。

senses.title: Not long ago
senses.definition: at a point in the near past, not long before now
senses.definitionCN: 在不久前的某个时点
senses.example: She recently joined the research team.
senses.exampleCN: 她最近加入了研究团队。
senses.why: The adjective recent means fresh in time, and -ly turns it into the adverb of a near past moment.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 recent 意为时间上新鲜的，加上 -ly 就成为表「不久前某一时点」的副词。

senses.title: Lately
senses.definition: during the period just before the present, seen as a stretch of time
senses.definitionCN: 在当下之前的一段时期里
senses.example: The weather has been unusually warm recently.
senses.exampleCN: 近来天气异常暖和。
senses.why: The same adverb covers a single moment and a stretch, because a recent period is made of recent moments.
senses.whyCN: 同一个副词既覆盖单个时点，也覆盖一段时期，因为「近期」正是由一个个「最近」组成。

senses.title: Newly in a role
senses.definition: at a time only shortly before now, especially after a change of status
senses.definitionCN: 在不久前，尤指身份刚发生改变之后
senses.example: The recently elected mayor promised reform.
senses.exampleCN: 新近当选的市长承诺推行改革。
senses.why: A change that has just happened leaves a person newly in a state, and the adverb marks that freshness of status.
senses.whyCN: 刚刚发生的变化让人处于一种新状态，这个副词正是标记身份的新鲜。

intro.en: Recently is the Latin adjective of freshness plus the English suffix of manner; a fresh moment becomes a fresh stretch of time.
intro.cn: recently 是拉丁语表新鲜的形容词加英语表方式的后缀；新鲜的瞬间由此变为新鲜的一段时间。

items.en: Recens meant fresh or just made, said of things still new.
items.cn: recens 意为新鲜的、刚做成的，用于仍然新的事物。

items.en: Old French recent carried the adjective into English without changing its sense.
items.cn: 古法语 recent 把这个形容词原样带入英语。

items.en: The native suffix -ly turns the adjective into an adverb of time and manner.
items.cn: 本族后缀 -ly 把形容词变为表时间与方式的副词。

items.en: Modern English uses recently for a near past moment and for the period just passed.
items.cn: 现代英语用 recently 指不久的过去时点，也指刚过去的一段时期。

items.en: The adverb widened from one moment to a whole stretch of recent time.
items.cn: 这个副词从单个瞬间扩展到整段近期时间。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adjective base and two words close in sound; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of the near past.
note.cn: 形近组收形容词原形与两个音近词；近义组收表「不久前」的副词。

entries.definition: In a proper and acceptable way.
In the time just before now.
Just now, in a fresh state.

normalIntro.en: The word is recent plus ly: what is fresh in time becomes an adverb of the near past.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 recent 加 ly：时间上新鲜的东西，变成表「不久前」的副词。

normal.en: Recent plus -ly: in a recent way, or in recent time.
normal.cn: recent 加 -ly：以最近的方式，或在最近的时间里。

normal.en: Until recently means up to a point not long ago.
normal.cn: until recently 意为直到不久前。

normal.en: Recently arrived describes a person or thing that has just come.
normal.cn: recently arrived 形容刚到的人或物。

normal.en: The comparison is more recently, never recentlier.
normal.cn: 比较级是 more recently，绝不是 recentlier。

normal.en: Keep the t before ly: recently, not recenly.
normal.cn: ly 前要保留 t：recently，而不是 recenly。

abstract.en: Recently is where memory and news overlap, still warm enough to matter.
abstract.cn: 「最近」是记忆与新闻重叠的地方，还热得足以重要。

abstract.en: A thing done recently can still be undone; that is its power.
abstract.cn: 最近做成的事仍可被撤回，这就是它的力量。

abstract.en: We call the near past recent because we have not finished living it.
abstract.cn: 我们称近过去为「最近」，因为我们还没把它过完。

examples.en: She recently joined the research team.
examples.cn: 她最近加入了研究团队。

examples.en: The weather has been unusually warm recently.
examples.cn: 近来天气异常暖和。

examples.en: The recently elected mayor promised reform.
examples.cn: 新近当选的市长承诺推行改革。

dict_mnemonic.text: recent（最近的）加 ly（地）：最近的时点、近来的一段日子，都是 recently。

root: 拉丁 recens（新鲜的）→ 英语 recent + 后缀 -ly → recently；同族有 recency、recentness。

sensesIntro.en: The core is temporal freshness; the senses move from one near moment to a recent stretch and to a newly changed status.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「时间上的新鲜」；义项从一个临近的时点，到一段近期，再到刚改变的身份。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a message on a screen stamped just now.
core.cn: 核心意象：屏幕上一条刚收到的消息，时间标着「刚刚」。

branches.en: a screen stamped just now
a warm week in a cold month
branches.cn: 寒冷月份里暖和的一周

branches.en: a newly elected mayor
a moment and a stretch of time
lately and newly

intro.en: A Latin adjective of freshness takes two English suffixes, one for state and one for manner, to become an adverb of time.
intro.cn: 表新鲜的拉丁形容词接上两个英语后缀，一个表状态，一个表方式，成为表时间的副词。

latinIntro.en: The base recens is Latin, and the comparative recentior explains the English degree forms.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 recens 是拉丁语，其比较级 recentior 解释了英语的比较形式。

definition_zh: 接待；招待会；前台；接收；反响
definition_en: the act of welcoming someone; a formal party; the desk where visitors arrive; the catching of signals; the response of an audience
core_image: 酒店大堂前台亮着灯的柜台
scene: 酒店大堂里，客人排在前台登记，行李箱靠在一旁。Guests waited at the reception desk for their room keys.
sceneCN: 这里 reception 修饰 desk，指「前台」（第 3 个义项：接待处）；句意为客人们在前台等候领取房卡。画面里可留意：亮着灯的前台柜台、靠在一旁的行李箱。

pos.zh: 接待；招待会；前台；接收；反响

senses.title: The act of welcoming someone
senses.definition: the act of greeting and welcoming a person who arrives
senses.definitionCN: 迎接并款待到来之人的行为
senses.example: The mayor gave the visitors a warm reception.
senses.exampleCN: 市长热情接待了来访者。
senses.why: The Latin noun receptio named a taking in, and a welcome is the human form of that taking in.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 receptio 指「收进来」，而迎接正是这种「收进来」的人际形式。

senses.title: A formal party
senses.definition: a formal social gathering held to welcome guests or mark an occasion
senses.definitionCN: 为迎接客人或纪念某事而举行的正式社交聚会
senses.example: They held a reception after the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 仪式结束后他们举行了一场招待会。
senses.why: A party is a welcome made visible in a room, with food, light, and guests standing together.
senses.whyCN: 招待会是把「欢迎」显现在一个房间里：食物、灯光与站在一起的宾客。

senses.title: The front desk
senses.definition: the desk or area where visitors are received in a hotel or office
senses.definitionCN: 酒店或办公楼里接待来访者的柜台或区域
senses.example: Guests waited at the reception desk for their room keys.
senses.exampleCN: 客人们在前台等候领取房卡。
senses.why: The place where receiving happens took the name of the act, so the desk itself became the reception.
senses.whyCN: 负责接待的地方借用了行为之名，于是柜台本身也被称为 reception。

senses.title: The catching of signals
senses.definition: the quality or act of receiving broadcast or electronic signals
senses.definitionCN: 接收广播或电子信号的行为或质量
senses.example: Poor reception made the call hard to follow.
senses.exampleCN: 信号不好，那通电话很难听清。
senses.why: A radio takes a signal in just as a host takes a guest in, so the technical sense grew from the same image.
senses.whyCN: 收音机收进信号，正如主人迎进客人，技术义正从同一形象生长出来。

senses.title: The response of an audience
senses.definition: the way people react to a performance, a book, or an idea
senses.definitionCN: 人们对于演出、书籍或观念的反应方式
senses.example: The novel received a mixed reception.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说得到的反响褒贬不一。
senses.why: To receive a work is to let it in and judge it, so reception came to mean the judgment of an audience.
senses.whyCN: 接受一部作品，就是让它进来并加以评判，于是 reception 引申为观众的评价。

intro.en: Reception is the noun of receiving: it names the act, the party, the desk, the signal, and the audience response.
intro.cn: reception 是「接收」的名词：它命名行为、宴会、柜台、信号，以及观众的反响。

items.en: Recipere meant to take in or receive, from re- and capere, to take.
items.cn: recipere 意为收进或接收，由 re- 与 capere（拿取）构成。

items.en: Receptio named the act of taking something or someone in.
items.cn: receptio 指把某物或某人收进来的行为。

items.en: Old French reception carried both the welcome and the technical sense.
items.cn: 古法语 reception 同时带有欢迎与技术两层含义。

items.en: Middle English reception named a welcome and a formal gathering.
items.cn: 中古英语 reception 指欢迎，也指正式聚会。

items.en: Modern English added the front desk, radio signals, and public response.
items.cn: 现代英语又加入了前台、无线电信号与公众反响。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns ending in the same sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for welcome, party, and response.
note.cn: 形近组收结尾音相同的名词；近义组收表欢迎、聚会与反响的词。

entries.definition: A greeting given to a newcomer.
A entrance hall or waiting area.

normalIntro.en: The word is receiving made into a noun, and the same act stretches from people to signals to reviews.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「接收」的名词化，同一个行为从人延伸到信号，再到评论。

normal.en: Receive plus -tion: the act of taking in.
normal.cn: receive 加 -tion：收进来这一行为。

normal.en: Reception desk is the first place a visitor meets in a hotel.
normal.cn: reception desk 是客人在酒店最先遇到的地方。

normal.en: A wedding reception is a party that welcomes guests after the vows.
normal.cn: wedding reception 是仪式后迎接宾客的宴会。

normal.en: Radio reception depends on the aerial, not on manners.
normal.cn: radio reception 取决于天线，而不取决于礼貌。

normal.en: A mixed reception means some liked the work and some did not.
normal.cn: a mixed reception 意为有人喜欢这部作品，有人不喜欢。

abstract.en: Every reception is a decision about what to let in.
abstract.cn: 每一次接待，都是关于让什么进来的决定。

abstract.en: A cold reception can freeze an idea before it grows.
abstract.cn: 冷淡的反响能在观念成长之前把它冻住。

abstract.en: The way a work is received is part of what the work becomes.
abstract.cn: 一部作品被接受的方式，构成了它最终的样子。

examples.en: The mayor gave the visitors a warm reception.
examples.cn: 市长热情接待了来访者。

examples.en: Guests waited at the reception desk for their room keys.
examples.cn: 客人们在前台等候领取房卡。

examples.en: The novel received a mixed reception.
examples.cn: 这部小说得到的反响褒贬不一。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（回）加 cept（拿取）加 ion（行为）：把客人接进来是接待，把信号接进来是接收，招待会也是把人迎来。

root: 拉丁 recipere（接收）→ 拉丁 receptio（接待）→ 古法语 reception → 英语 reception；同族有 receive、receiver、receptive。

sensesIntro.en: The core is taking someone or something in; the senses move from a welcome to a party, a desk, a signal, and a public response.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把某人或某物收进来」；义项从欢迎，到宴会、前台、信号，再到公众反响。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit desk in a hotel lobby, keys laid out for arriving guests.
core.cn: 核心意象：酒店大堂里亮着灯的前台，房卡摆给到来的客人。

branches.en: a handshake at the door
candles and guests in a hall
keys waiting on a counter
an aerial on the roof
a row of reviews in a paper

intro.en: The family is built on the Latin verb of taking, and the noun ending turns the act into a place, an event, and a response.
intro.cn: 这个词族建立在拉丁语的「拿取」动词上，名词词尾把行为变成场所、事件与反响。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is recipere and its noun receptio; the ending -tion came through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 recipere 及其名词 receptio；词尾 -tion 经法语而来。

definition_en: a period when trade and industry shrink; the act of moving back; the slow withdrawal of water or ice
core_image: 退潮后的沙滩上留下一道道水痕
scene: 工厂车间贴出停工通知，工人排队走出大门。Many factories closed during the recession.
sceneCN: 这里 recession 是「经济衰退」（第 1 个义项：工商业萎缩的时期）；句意为许多工厂在衰退期间倒闭。画面里可留意：停工的车间、贴出的通知。

senses.title: A shrinking economy
senses.definition: a period in which trade, industry, and output fall for several months
senses.definitionCN: 贸易、工业与产出连续数月下滑的时期
senses.example: Many factories closed during the recession.
senses.exampleCN: 许多工厂在衰退期间倒闭。
senses.why: An economy that goes backward is pictured as a tide going out, and the noun for that backward movement became the name of the slump.
senses.whyCN: 往回走的经济被描绘成退潮，而表这种后退的名词成了萧条的称呼。

senses.title: The act of moving back
senses.definition: the act of withdrawing or stepping back from a position
senses.definitionCN: 从某一位置撤回或后退的行为
senses.example: The army's recession from the border was orderly.
senses.exampleCN: 军队从边境的后撤井然有序。
senses.why: Latin recedere means to go back, and the noun kept the plain physical sense before economics borrowed it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 recedere 意为往回走，名词先保留了这个朴素的物理义，后来才被经济学借用。

senses.title: The slow withdrawal of water or ice
senses.definition: the gradual movement back of a tide, a glacier, or a flood
senses.definitionCN: 潮水、冰川或洪水的逐渐回退
senses.example: The recession of the glacier exposed bare rock.
senses.exampleCN: 冰川的退去露出了裸露的岩石。
senses.why: Water and ice going back are the same movement as an army going back, so the word covers natural withdrawal.
senses.whyCN: 水与冰的回退，和军队的后撤是同一种运动，因此这个词也涵盖自然的退去。

intro.en: Recession is a Latin going-back noun: first a step backward, then a tide, then a whole economy.
intro.cn: recession 是拉丁语表「往回走」的名词：先是后退一步，再是退潮，最后是整个经济。

items.en: Cedere meant to go or yield, the movement at the heart of the family.
items.cn: cedere 意为走或让出，是整个词族的核心动作。

items.en: Recedere added re-, back, to cedere, giving the sense of going backward.
items.cn: recedere 在 cedere 前加 re-（回），得到「往回走」的意思。

items.en: Recessus, the noun of the verb, named a backward movement or a withdrawn place.
items.cn: 动词的名词形式 recessus 指后退的运动或退隐之处。

items.en: French recession carried the noun into English with its physical sense intact.
items.cn: 法语 récession 把这个名词带入英语，物理义完好保留。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word became the standard term for a shrinking economy.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这个词成为经济萎缩的标准术语。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns ending in the same sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for economic decline.
note.cn: 形近组收结尾音相同的名词；近义组收表经济下滑的词。

entries.definition: A line of people moving forward.
A long period of low activity.
A gradual loss of strength or value.

normalIntro.en: The word is a going back: first a tide, then an army, then the whole economy.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「往回走」：先退潮，再撤军，最后是整个经济。

normal.en: Re plus cess plus ion: going back again and again.
normal.cn: re 加 cess 加 ion：一再往回走。

normal.en: Recession and recede share the same going-back root.
normal.cn: recession 与 recede 共享同一个「往回走」的词根。

normal.en: An economy in recession is a tide going out.
normal.cn: 处于衰退的经济，就是正在退去的潮水。

normal.en: Economic recession is the most common modern use.
normal.cn: economic recession 是当代最常见的用法。

normal.en: Two c and two s in succession: recession is easy to misspell.
normal.cn: succession 里有两个 c 两个 s，recession 也容易拼错。

abstract.en: A recession is a society discovering what it cannot afford.
abstract.cn: 衰退是一个社会发现自己负担不起什么的过程。

abstract.en: What goes out with the tide leaves marks that show where it stood.
abstract.cn: 随潮退去的东西会留下痕迹，标出它曾经的位置。

abstract.en: Every retreat is also a chance to see the ground clearly.
abstract.cn: 每一次后退，也是看清地面的机会。

examples.en: Many factories closed during the recession.
examples.cn: 许多工厂在衰退期间倒闭。

examples.en: The recession of the glacier exposed bare rock.
examples.cn: 冰川的退去露出了裸露的岩石。

examples.en: The company survived two recessions in a decade.
examples.cn: 这家公司在十年里挺过了两次衰退。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（回）加 cess（走）加 ion（行为）：往回走就是后退；整个经济往回走，就是衰退。

root: 拉丁 cedere（走）→ recedere（往回走）→ recessus（后退）→ 法语 récession → 英语 recession；同族有 recede、recess、recessive。

sensesIntro.en: The core is movement backward; the senses move from an army stepping back to a tide withdrawing and to a shrinking economy.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「向后退」；义项从军队后撤，到潮水退去，再到经济萎缩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water marks left on a beach after the tide has gone back.
core.cn: 核心意象：退潮后的沙滩上留下一道道水痕。

branches.en: a closed factory gate
a line of soldiers stepping back
a glacier leaving bare rock
a retreat and a shrinking economy
an army and a tide both going back

intro.en: A Latin verb of going takes a prefix of return and a noun ending, and the family spreads from footsteps to markets.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的「走」动词接上表「回」的前缀与名词词尾，这个词族从脚步延伸到市场。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is cedere, to go; re- turns it back, and -io makes the movement a noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 cedere（走）；re- 使其转向回，-io 把这一运动变成名词。

definition_en: to think or believe; to calculate or estimate; to count on something; to settle an account
core_image: 渔夫坐在船头，用手指节在木板上比划数目
scene: 渔夫坐在船头，凭经验数着今天的收获。I reckon it will rain before noon.
sceneCN: 这里 reckon 是「认为」（第 1 个义项：觉得、估计）；句意为我认为中午前会下雨。画面里可留意：船头数收成的渔夫、比划的手指。

senses.title: To think or believe
senses.definition: to think that something is true or likely
senses.definitionCN: 认为某事为真或很可能发生
senses.example: I reckon it will rain before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 我认为中午前会下雨。
senses.why: Counting a thing as true became the everyday sense of believing, because a judgment is a sum we make in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 把一件事算作真的，就成了日常的「相信」，因为判断正是心里做的一次加法。

senses.title: To calculate or estimate
senses.definition: to work out an amount by counting or judging
senses.definitionCN: 通过数算或判断算出某个数量
senses.example: The builder reckoned the cost at ten thousand pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 施工方估算成本为一万英镑。
senses.why: The oldest sense is to count in order, and adding up numbers is still the clearest use of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是按顺序数算，而把数字加起来仍是这个动词最清楚的用法。

senses.title: To count on something
senses.definition: to rely on something happening or being available
senses.definitionCN: 依赖某事发生或可得到
senses.example: We reckoned on fine weather for the picnic.
senses.exampleCN: 我们指望野餐时天气晴好。
senses.why: To reckon on is to put something into your sum as certain, and hope is a kind of accounting.
senses.whyCN: reckon on 就是把某件事当作确定的项计入你的账里，而期待本身就是一种算计。

senses.title: To settle an account
senses.definition: to work out and settle what is owed between people
senses.definitionCN: 算出并结清人与人之间应付的款项
senses.example: The clerk reckoned the bill at the end of the day.
senses.exampleCN: 店员在一天结束时结清了账目。
senses.why: A reckoning is the moment when the numbers are finally added and the account is closed.
senses.whyCN: reckoning 就是数字终于加完、账目就此结清的时刻。

intro.en: Reckon is a native English verb of recounting: telling in order, counting in order, and finally judging.
intro.cn: reckon 是英语本族表「讲述」的动词：按顺序讲述，按顺序数算，最后成为判断。

items.en: Gerecenian meant to recount or explain, telling a matter in order.
items.cn: gerecenian 意为讲述或解释，把事情按顺序说出来。

items.en: From recounting came the sense of counting and adding up amounts.
items.cn: 从「讲述」引申出「数算」与「加总」的意思。

items.en: Middle English reknen meant both to count and to think.
items.cn: 中古英语 reknen 既指数算，也指思考。

items.en: Counting something as true became the everyday sense of believing.
items.cn: 把某事算作真的，成为日常的「相信」。

items.en: Modern English uses reckon for thinking, estimating, relying, and settling accounts.
items.cn: 现代英语用 reckon 表认为、估算、指望与结账。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words close in sound; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of thinking, counting, and estimating.
note.cn: 形近组收读音相近的短词；近义组收表思考、计算与估算的动词。

normalIntro.en: The word began as telling in order, became counting in order, and ended as judging in the mind.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从按顺序讲述开始，变为按顺序数算，最后成为心里的判断。

normal.en: Reckon sounds like reckoning: adding numbers until a total appears.
normal.cn: reckon 与 reckoning 同源：一直加数，直到总数出现。

normal.en: I reckon is the spoken way to say I think.
normal.cn: I reckon 是口语里的「我认为」。

normal.en: Reckon with means to take something into your sum.
normal.cn: reckon with 意为把某事计入你的账里。

normal.en: Reckon on means to rely on it being there.
normal.cn: reckon on 意为指望它在。

normal.en: Reckon up the bill is to add all the items together.
normal.cn: reckon up the bill 就是把所有项目加起来。

abstract.en: To reckon is to make the world add up, even when the numbers resist.
abstract.cn: 估算就是让世界加得起来，即使数字并不配合。

abstract.en: Every reckoning is a moment when someone decides what counts.
abstract.cn: 每一次清算，都是某人决定「什么才算数」的时刻。

abstract.en: Reckless people refuse the sum that others cannot stop making.
abstract.cn: 鲁莽的人拒绝去做别人停不下来的那道加法。

examples.en: I reckon it will rain before noon.
examples.cn: 我认为中午前会下雨。

examples.en: The builder reckoned the cost at ten thousand pounds.
examples.cn: 施工方估算成本为一万英镑。

examples.en: We reckoned on fine weather for the picnic.
examples.cn: 我们指望野餐时天气晴好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「渔夫用指节在船板上数数」：数着数着，心里就有了判断——认为、估算都由此而来。

root: 古英语 gerecenian（讲述、数算）→ 中古英语 reknen → 现代英语 reckon；同族有 reckoning、reckless。

sensesIntro.en: The core is counting in order; the senses move from calculation to expectation, to judgment, and to a settled account.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「按序数算」；义项从计算，到期待，到判断，再到结清的账目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fisherman at the bow counting his catch on the planks.
core.cn: 核心意象：渔夫坐在船头，在木板上数着收成。

branches.en: a fisherman guessing the weather
a builder's estimate on paper
branches.cn: 施工方写在纸上的估算

branches.en: a picnic planned on fine weather
branches.cn: 指望晴天而安排的野餐

branches.en: a bill settled at the day's end
branches.cn: 一天结束时结清的账单

branches.en: a judgment reached and an amount worked out
branches.cn: 得出的判断与算出的数目

intro.en: The word is native and short, and its small family is built on the idea of counting and on the suffix that turns it into a noun.
intro.cn: 这个词短小且为本族词，其不大的词族建立在「数算」的观念与把它名词化的后缀上。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source is recorded; reckon is a native Germanic verb.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠的拉丁语来源；reckon 是日耳曼语本族动词。

definition_en: the act of knowing someone or something again; the acceptance of a fact; public praise; matching by machine
core_image: 门禁摄像头扫过脸庞，屏幕跳出名字
scene: 门禁摄像头扫过一张脸，屏幕上跳出熟悉的名字。The system uses facial recognition to unlock the door.
sceneCN: 这里 recognition 是「识别」（第 4 个义项：机器认出对象）；句意为系统用人脸识别来开门。画面里可留意：扫过脸庞的摄像头、跳出的名字。

senses.title: The act of knowing again
senses.definition: the act of identifying someone or something as already known
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物辨认出为已知对象的行为
senses.example: He stared at her without recognition.
senses.exampleCN: 他盯着她，却没有认出她。
senses.why: Recognoscere meant to know again, and the noun names that second knowing.
senses.whyCN: recognoscere 意为「再一次认识」，这个名词正指这第二次认识。

senses.title: The acceptance of a fact
senses.definition: the act of admitting that something is true or official
senses.definitionCN: 承认某事为真或为官方事实的行为
senses.example: The new state won official recognition.
senses.exampleCN: 这个新国家获得了官方承认。
senses.why: To know again is also to admit what one already knew, so the word covers formal acceptance.
senses.whyCN: 「再一次知道」也是承认自己早已知道的事，因此这个词涵盖正式承认。

senses.title: Public praise
senses.definition: the appreciation and honour that a person or a work receives from others
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或一部作品从他人那里得到的欣赏与荣誉
senses.example: She received recognition for her research.
senses.exampleCN: 她的研究获得了认可。
senses.why: When a group knows a person's worth again and again, that knowledge becomes honour.
senses.whyCN: 当一个群体一次次看见某个人的价值，这种认识就变成荣誉。

senses.title: Matching by machine
senses.definition: the process by which a computer identifies a face, a voice, or a pattern
senses.definitionCN: 计算机辨认面孔、声音或图案的过程
senses.example: The system uses facial recognition to unlock the door.
senses.exampleCN: 系统用人脸识别来开门。
senses.why: A machine that matches a pattern knows it again, so the old word fits the new technology.
senses.whyCN: 能匹配图案的机器，就是「再一次认出」它，于是旧词恰好适用于新技术。

intro.en: Recognition is the noun of knowing again: a face, a fact, a person's worth, and a digital pattern.
intro.cn: recognition 是「再次认识」的名词：一张脸、一个事实、一个人的价值，以及一段数字图案。

items.en: Cognoscere meant to know or learn, the root of cognition and recognition.
items.cn: cognoscere 意为认识或得知，是 cognition 与 recognition 的词根。

items.en: Recognoscere added re-, again, to cognoscere, giving the sense of knowing again.
items.cn: recognoscere 在 cognoscere 前加 re-（再次），得到「再一次认识」。

items.en: Recognitio named the act of calling something back to mind.
items.cn: recognitio 指把某物重新唤回心里的行为。

items.en: Old French reconnaissance carried the word into English as a survey or a knowing again.
items.cn: 古法语 reconnaissance 把这个词带入英语，指勘察或再次确认。

items.en: Modern English uses recognition for memory, for diplomacy, for honour, and for machine matching.
items.cn: 现代英语用 recognition 表记忆、外交、荣誉，以及机器匹配。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns ending in the same sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for identification and approval.
note.cn: 形近组收结尾音相同的名词；近义组收表辨认与认可的词。

entries.definition: A firm belief or a court ruling.
The starting of a fire or engine.
The act of naming what something is.
The act of admitting or thanking.
The act of receiving something as valid.

normalIntro.en: The word is knowing plus again: the second knowing is recognition.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「知道」加「再一次」：第二次知道，就是 recognition。

normal.en: Cognition is knowing; recognition is knowing again.
normal.cn: cognition 是知道，recognition 是再一次知道。

normal.en: Beyond recognition means changed so much that you cannot know it again.
normal.cn: beyond recognition 意为变化太大，再也认不出来。

normal.en: In recognition of is the phrase on a prize or a certificate.
normal.cn: in recognition of 是奖状上的常用短语。

normal.en: Facial recognition is a machine doing the knowing again.
normal.cn: facial recognition 是机器在做「再一次知道」。

normal.en: Keep the g in the middle: recognition, not recongition.
normal.cn: 中间的 g 要保留：recognition，而不是 recongition。

abstract.en: Recognition is the moment when the past and the present meet in one look.
abstract.cn: 认出，是过去与当下在一个目光里相遇的瞬间。

abstract.en: To be recognized is to be told that one's existence counts.
abstract.cn: 被认出，就是被告知自己的存在算数。

abstract.en: A machine that recognizes faces is learning the oldest human act.
abstract.cn: 识别人脸的机器，正在学习最古老的人类行为。

examples.en: He stared at her without recognition.
examples.cn: 他盯着她，却没有认出她。

examples.en: The new state won official recognition.
examples.cn: 这个新国家获得了官方承认。

examples.en: She received recognition for her research.
examples.cn: 她的研究获得了认可。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（再）加 cognition（认知）：再一次认出，就是 recognition——认出、承认、赏识都由此而来。

root: 拉丁 cognoscere（认识）→ recognoscere（再认识）→ recognitio（认出）→ 古法语 reconnaissance → 英语 recognition；同族有 recognize、recognizable。

sensesIntro.en: The core is knowing again; the senses move from a face to a fact, to honour, and to a machine match.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「再一次认识」；义项从一张脸，到事实，到荣誉，再到机器匹配。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a camera sweeping a face, a name appearing on the screen.
core.cn: 核心意象：摄像头扫过脸庞，屏幕上跳出名字。

branches.en: a friend seen across a street
a treaty signed by two states
a medal placed in a hand
a screen showing a name
a human and a machine both knowing again
branches.cn: 人与机器都在「再一次认识」

intro.en: The word is built on the Latin verb of knowing, with a prefix of repetition and a noun ending of result.
intro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语的「认识」动词上，加上表重复的前缀与表结果的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is cognoscere, to know, changed by re- and named by -itio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 cognoscere（认识），由 re- 加以改变，并由 -itio 名词化。

definition_en: to identify someone or something as known; to admit a fact; to give credit or approval; to match a pattern by machine
core_image: 街上有人叫住你，你回头认出是老同学
scene: 街上有人叫住你，你回头看了两秒才认出对方。I did not recognize him until he called my name.
sceneCN: 这里 recognize 是「认出」（第 1 个义项：认出认识的人或物）；句意为直到他叫我的名字，我才认出他。画面里可留意：回头张望、叫住你的那只手。

senses.title: To know someone again
senses.definition: to identify a person or a thing as one already known
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物辨认出为已知对象
senses.example: I did not recognize him until he called my name.
senses.exampleCN: 直到他叫我的名字，我才认出他。
senses.why: Recognoscere meant to know again, and the English verb keeps that moment of a second meeting.
senses.whyCN: recognoscere 意为「再一次认识」，英语动词保留了「第二次相遇」的瞬间。

senses.title: To admit a fact
senses.definition: to accept that something is true, often reluctantly
senses.definitionCN: 接受某事为真，常带不情愿
senses.example: The government finally recognized the problem.
senses.exampleCN: 政府终于承认了这个问题。
senses.why: To know again is also to admit what one already knew, so the word covers reluctant acceptance.
senses.whyCN: 「再一次知道」也是承认自己早已知道的事，因此这个词涵盖不情愿的接受。

senses.title: To give credit
senses.definition: to show appreciation for a person's work or value
senses.definitionCN: 对某人的工作或价值表示欣赏
senses.example: Her work was recognized by the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 她的工作得到了委员会的认可。
senses.why: When others know a person's worth again and again, that knowing becomes public credit.
senses.whyCN: 当他人一次次看见某个人的价值，这种认识就成了公开的认可。

senses.title: To match a pattern by machine
senses.definition: to identify a face, a voice, or a shape by computer
senses.definitionCN: 由计算机辨认面孔、声音或形状
senses.example: The app can recognize handwriting.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用能识别人手写的字。
senses.why: A machine that matches a pattern knows it again, so the old verb fits the new technology.
senses.whyCN: 能匹配图案的机器，就是「再一次认出」它，于是旧动词恰好适用于新技术。

intro.en: Recognize is the Latin verb of knowing again, carried through French and given an English spelling.
intro.cn: recognize 是拉丁语「再一次认识」的动词，经法语传来，并换上英语拼写。

items.en: Cognoscere meant to know or learn, the root of the whole family.
items.cn: cognoscere 意为认识或得知，是整个词族的词根。

items.en: Recognoscere added re-, again, giving the sense of knowing a second time.
items.cn: recognoscere 加上 re-（再次），得到「第二次认识」。

items.en: Old French carried the verb into English with the same re- prefix.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词带入英语，re- 前缀保持不变。

items.en: Middle English recognizen covered both identifying and admitting.
items.cn: 中古英语 recognizen 既指辨认，也指承认。

items.en: American spelling settled on -ize, while British English also accepts -ise.
items.cn: 美式拼写定为 -ize，英式英语也接受 -ise。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs ending in the same sound; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of identifying and approving.
note.cn: 形近组收结尾音相同的动词；近义组收表辨认与认可的词。

entries.definition: To arrange something in a new way.
To recognize the value of something.

normalIntro.en: The word is knowing plus again, and the same act covers a face, a fact, a person's value, and a pattern.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「知道」加「再一次」，同一个行为覆盖一张脸、一个事实、一个人的价值，以及一段图案。

normal.en: Recognize is cognition with a re- in front and an -ize on the end.
normal.cn: recognize 就是 cognition 前面加 re-，后面加 -ize。

normal.en: Recognize a face is the picture; recognize a fact is the extension.
normal.cn: recognize a face 是画面，recognize a fact 是引申。

normal.en: Widely recognized is a common phrase on a plaque or a report.
normal.cn: widely recognized 是奖牌或报告上的常见说法。

normal.en: British English also writes recognise, with s instead of z.
normal.cn: 英式英语也写作 recognise，用 s 代替 z。

normal.en: Do not drop the g: recognize, recognized, recognizing.
normal.cn: 不要漏掉 g：recognize、recognized、recognizing。

abstract.en: To recognize is to let the past prove that it still lives.
abstract.cn: 认出，就是让过去证明它仍然活着。

abstract.en: Recognizing a fault is the first honest act a person can perform.
abstract.cn: 承认错误，是一个人能做的第一件诚实之事。

abstract.en: The one who recognizes another gives that person a place in the world.
abstract.cn: 认出他人的人，等于给了对方一个在世界上的一席之地。

examples.en: I did not recognize him until he called my name.
examples.cn: 直到他叫我的名字，我才认出他。

examples.en: The government finally recognized the problem.
examples.cn: 政府终于承认了这个问题。

examples.en: The app can recognize handwriting.
examples.cn: 这款应用能识别人手写的字。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（再）加 cognize（认识）：再认识一次，就是认出；把已知的事实再确认，就是承认。

root: 拉丁 cognoscere（认识）→ recognoscere（再认识）→ 中古英语 recognizen → 英语 recognize；同族有 recognition、recognizable。

sensesIntro.en: The core is knowing again; the senses move from a face to a fact, to public credit, and to a machine match.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「再一次认识」；义项从一张脸，到事实，到公开认可，再到机器匹配。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stranger calling your name, and a face becoming familiar.
core.cn: 核心意象：陌生人叫出你的名字，一张脸忽然变得熟悉。

branches.en: a face turning in the street
a report admitting a fault
a prize handed over
an app reading handwriting
a person known and a person honoured
branches.cn: 认出一个也表彰一个人

intro.en: The Latin verb of knowing takes a prefix of repetition and an English verb ending, and the spellings vary by region.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的「认识」动词接上表重复的前缀与英语动词词尾，拼写因地区而异。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is cognoscere, and re- marks the second knowing; the ending -ize came through French and English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 cognoscere，re- 标记第二次认识；词尾 -ize 经法语与英语形成。

definition_zh: 推荐；建议；使显得可取；托付
definition_en: to praise something as worth choosing; to advise a course of action; to make something attractive; to entrust formally
core_image: 店员把一本书递到顾客手里，说值得一读
scene: 书店里，店员从架上抽出一本小说递到顾客手里。Librarians often recommend books to new readers.
sceneCN: 这里 recommend 是「推荐」（第 1 个义项：称赞某物值得选择）；句意为图书管理员常向新读者推荐书籍。画面里可留意：递到手里的书、架上的书脊。

pos.zh: 推荐；建议；使显得可取；托付

senses.title: To praise as worth choosing
senses.definition: to speak in favour of something and suggest that others choose it
senses.definitionCN: 称赞某物并建议他人选择它
senses.example: Librarians often recommend books to new readers.
senses.exampleCN: 图书管理员常向新读者推荐书籍。
senses.why: Commendare meant to praise and entrust, and re- strengthened the praise, so the word pictures praise offered for a choice.
senses.whyCN: commendare 意为称赞与托付，re- 加强了称赞，因此这个词描绘为供人选择而给出的赞美。

senses.title: To advise a course of action
senses.definition: to tell someone what you think they should do
senses.definitionCN: 告诉某人你认为他应当怎么做
senses.example: Doctors recommend regular exercise.
senses.exampleCN: 医生建议经常锻炼。
senses.why: Praise and advice are close: what is worth choosing is also what one should do.
senses.whyCN: 称赞与建议很接近：值得选择的东西，也正是应当去做的事。

senses.title: To make something attractive
senses.definition: to give a place or a plan qualities that invite approval
senses.definitionCN: 赋予某地或某方案令人赞许的品质
senses.example: The quiet garden recommends the house to buyers.
senses.exampleCN: 安静的花园让这所房子更讨买家喜欢。
senses.why: When a place or a plan makes itself pleasing, it is as if it praised itself, and the verb covers that self-praise.
senses.whyCN: 当某地或某方案显得讨人喜欢，它就像在自我称赞，这个动词正涵盖这种自我推荐。

senses.title: To entrust formally
senses.definition: to hand a person or a task into someone's care with confidence
senses.definitionCN: 放心地把人或任务交给他人照管
senses.example: She recommended her children to her sister's care.
senses.exampleCN: 她把孩子托付给姐姐照看。
senses.why: The Latin root also carried the sense of entrusting, because praising someone is a way of handing a task to them.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根也带「托付」义，因为称赞某人，正是把任务交给他的方式。

intro.en: Recommend joins praise to trust: the Latin verb meant both to commend and to entrust, and English kept both directions.
intro.cn: recommend 把称赞与信任连在一起：拉丁动词既指称赞也指托付，英语保留了这两个方向。

items.en: Mandare meant to hand over or command, the root of the whole family.
items.cn: mandare 意为交出或命令，是整个词族的词根。

items.en: Commendare joined com- with mandare and meant to entrust or praise.
items.cn: commendare 由 com- 与 mandare 组成，意为托付或称赞。

items.en: Recommendare strengthened the praise with re- and meant to recommend.
items.cn: recommendare 用 re- 加强称赞，意为推荐。

items.en: French recommander carried the word into English with both senses.
items.cn: 法语 recommander 把称赞与托付两义一起带入英语。

items.en: Modern English added the sense of a place or plan that makes itself attractive.
items.cn: 现代英语又加入了「某地或方案自我推荐」的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs built on the same Latin root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of advising and endorsing.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词根上的动词；近义组收表建议与支持的动词。

entries.definition: To tell someone what is wise.

normalIntro.en: The word is a second praising: re- adds strength to commend, and praise becomes a suggestion.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「再一次称赞」：re- 为 commend 加强语气，称赞于是变成建议。

normal.en: Re plus commend: praise something twice, and you recommend it.
normal.cn: re 加 commend：把某物称赞两次，就是推荐它。

normal.en: Recommend doing is the pattern; recommend to do is not standard.
normal.cn: recommend doing 是固定结构，recommend to do 不合标准。

normal.en: Highly recommended means many people praise it.
normal.cn: highly recommended 意为很多人称赞它。

normal.en: A doctor recommends a habit; a friend recommends a film.
normal.cn: 医生建议一种习惯，朋友推荐一部电影。

normal.en: Keep the double m: re + commend gives recommend.
normal.cn: 注意双写 m：re 加 commend 构成 recommend。

abstract.en: To recommend is to lend your own judgment to another person.
abstract.cn: 推荐，就是把自己的判断借给别人。

abstract.en: A recommendation is a small promise that the other person will not regret it.
abstract.cn: 推荐是一个小小的承诺：对方不会后悔。

abstract.en: What we recommend reveals what we value more than what we say.
abstract.cn: 我们推荐什么，比我们说什么更能暴露我们的价值。

examples.en: Librarians often recommend books to new readers.
examples.cn: 图书管理员常向新读者推荐书籍。

examples.en: Doctors recommend regular exercise.
examples.cn: 医生建议经常锻炼。

examples.en: The quiet garden recommends the house to buyers.
examples.cn: 安静的花园让这所房子更讨买家喜欢。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（再）加 commend（称赞）：一再称赞，就是推荐；把值得的东西说给别人听，也就是建议。

root: 拉丁 mandare（托付）→ commendare（称赞、托付）→ recommendare（推荐）→ 法语 recommander → 英语 recommend；同族有 recommendation。

sensesIntro.en: The core is praise offered to guide a choice; the senses move from praising a thing to advising an act, to self-praise, and to formal entrusting.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「为引导选择而给出的称赞」；义项从称赞某物，到建议行动，到自我推荐，再到正式托付。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a book taken from a shelf and placed in another person's hands.
core.cn: 核心意象：从架上抽出一本书，放进另一个人手里。

branches.en: a book handed across a counter
branches.cn: 从柜台递过来的一本书

branches.en: a doctor naming a habit
a garden that sells itself
children placed in a sister's care
branches.cn: 孩子被托付给姐姐照看

branches.en: praise and advice in one act
branches.cn: 称赞与建议合为一个动作

intro.en: The family is built on a Latin verb of handing over, and praise grows out of the act of entrusting.
intro.cn: 这个词族建立在拉丁语表「交出」的动词上，称赞从托付这一行为中生长出来。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is mandare, to hand over; com- and re- shape it into commend and recommend.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 mandare（交出）；com- 与 re- 把它塑造成 commend 与 recommend。

definition_en: a suggestion that something is worth choosing; a letter praising a person; formal advice in a report
core_image: 教授在办公桌上写一封带签名的信
scene: 教授坐在办公桌旁，把写好的信装进信封，签上名字。She wrote a letter of recommendation for her student.
sceneCN: 这里 recommendation 是「推荐信」（第 2 个义项：为某人说好话的书面材料）；句意为她为学生写了一封推荐信。画面里可留意：桌上的信纸、签好的名字。

senses.title: A suggestion to choose
senses.definition: a piece of advice that something is worth choosing or doing
senses.definitionCN: 认为某物值得选择或某事值得做的一条建议
senses.example: The committee made several recommendations.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会提出了若干建议。
senses.why: The noun turns the act of praising into a piece of advice that another person can follow.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词把称赞的行为变成一条他人可以照做的建议。

senses.title: A letter of praise
senses.definition: a written statement praising a person's qualities, usually for a job or a school
senses.definitionCN: 称赞某人品质的书面材料，通常用于求职或升学
senses.example: She wrote a letter of recommendation for her student.
senses.exampleCN: 她为学生写了一封推荐信。
senses.why: When praise is written down and signed, it becomes a document that travels without its author.
senses.whyCN: 当称赞被写下并签名，它就成了一份能脱离作者而流转的文件。

senses.title: Formal advice in a report
senses.definition: an official proposal made by a committee, an inspector, or a report
senses.definitionCN: 由委员会、检查员或报告提出的正式提议
senses.example: The report's recommendations were accepted by the board.
senses.exampleCN: 报告的建议被董事会采纳了。
senses.why: A committee that praises a policy in public is making a formal recommendation, and the word widened to official advice.
senses.whyCN: 委员会公开称赞某项政策，就是在提出正式建议，于是这个词扩展到官方意见。

intro.en: Recommendation is recommend plus the noun ending -ation: praise and advice turned into a thing one can hold.
intro.cn: recommendation 是 recommend 加名词词尾 -ation：称赞与建议变成了可以拿在手里的东西。

items.en: Mandare meant to hand over, the root behind the whole family.
items.cn: mandare 意为交出，是整个词族背后的词根。

items.en: Commendare joined praise to entrusting, giving both senses to the family.
items.cn: commendare 把称赞与托付结合，为词族带来两层含义。
